I'm a machine learning engineer who works on LLM serving: the systems that take a
trained model and turn it into something fast, affordable, and reliable enough to
build products on.

Over the last 8+ years I've shipped production ML across very different settings:
multi-node LLM inference and serving runtimes in the cloud, real-time ML systems for
insurance, deep learning models on aerial imagery, and user-facing NLP, computer
vision, and AutoML tools used by non-technical people.

The thread through all of it is making complicated systems understandable. I've given
talks at Alteryx Inspire and Data Connect West, built visualizations that explain
model behavior to non-experts, and automated documentation so it stays accurate.

**What I write about here:** how LLM serving actually works, explained for
application engineers, platform teams, and technical PMs building agents and apps on
top of it, with a focus on the decisions that change latency and cost.

*Views are my own and don't represent my employer.*
